**Group:** Ciliates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A small planktonic ciliate whose body is divided by an equatorial girdle of cilia into anterior and posterior regions, with tentacle-like cirri and extrusomes and a characteristic fast, jerky jumping swimming behaviour. Mesodinium rubrum (Myrionecta rubra) is reddish-brown from sequestered cryptophyte plastids and forms non-toxic red tides. Key features: small cell, equatorial ciliary girdle, often reddish, distinctive jumping motion.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **ciliate** | Label Mesodinium for the small girdled ciliate (often reddish, jumping); use the generic Ciliate class for other naked ciliates. |
| **tiarina** | Tiarina is a larger fusiform (spindle) ciliate with lengthwise ciliary rows; Mesodinium is small with an equatorial ciliary girdle. |
